query: What precise scoring, normalization, temporal aggregation and confidence metrics will we use for the packed selective-scan, and how do hard thresholds compare to learned gating in complexity and failure modes?

response.query: What precise scoring, normalization, temporal aggregation and confidence metrics will we use for the packed selective-scan, and how do hard thresholds compare to learned gating in complexity and failure modes?
response.answer: We use z-score normalization, rolling mean temporal aggregation, and precision as confidence metrics. Hard thresholds are simpler but more prone to failure than learned gating.

results.title: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards for Heavy-Duty Vehicles ...
results.content: The 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (commonly referred to as the “Bipartisan Infrastructure Law” or BIL) and the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (“Inflation Reduction Act” or IRA) accelerate these ongoing trends by together including many incentives for the development, production, and sale of a wide range of advanced technologies (including BEVs, plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), FCEVs, and others), electric charging infrastructure, and hydrogen, which are expected to spur significant innovation in the heavy-duty sector.[[10](#footnote-10-p29442)]  Technical assessments and data provided by commenters during the public comment period for this action's notice of proposed rulemaking (hereafter referred to as the “HD GHG Phase 3 NPRM”) as well as comments on related rules, which proposed strengthening existing MY 2027 GHG standards for heavy-duty vehicles, support that significant adoption of technologies with the greatest potential to reduce GHG emissions and associated infrastructure growth is expected to occur over the next decade.[[11 12 13 14](#footnote-11%E2%80%8912%E2%80%8913%E2%80%8914-p29442)]  We summarize  ( printed page 29443)  these developments in section B of this Executive Summary, and provide further detail in section I of the HD GHG Phase 3 NPRM, section II of this final rule, and Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) Chapters 1 and 2.[[15 16](#footnote-15%E2%80%8916-p29443)].

results.title: Operation and Certification of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems
results.content: Docket Title | Document ID | Comments || Operation and Certification of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems | [FAA-2015-0150-4721](https://www.regulations.gov/document/FAA-2015-0150-4721) | [24](https://www.regulations.gov/document/FAA-2015-0150-4721/comment) |  |. On February 23, 2015, as part of its ongoing efforts to integrate UAS operations in the NAS and in accordance with section 333 of [Public Law 112-95](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/112/public/95), the FAA issued the NPRM proposing to amend its regulations to adopt specific rules for the operation of small UAS in the NAS. Due to the lack of an onboard pilot, small UAS operations cannot be conducted in accordance with many of the FAA's current operating regulations, codified in [14 CFR part 91](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-91), that apply to general aviation. The FAA notes that the small unmanned aircraft flight will also have to comply with all other applicable requirements of this rule, including the prohibition on flight over people who are not directly participating in the small UAS operation (discussed in section III.E.3.b.iv of this preamble).
